name: Early Experiments & Mainframes
description: Before consumer electronics existed, scientists and university researchers repurposed military radar tubes and mainframe supercomputers to build the world's very first interactive virtual experiences.
curatorNotes: Games in this era were largely academic demonstrations or military engineering curiosities, running on machines that filled entire rooms like the PDP-1 and Nimrod.

name: First Generation & Dawn of Arcades
description: Ralph Baer's Magnavox Odyssey creates the home console industry, while Nolan Bushnell and Ted Dabney forge Atari and launch Pong into bars and arcades across the world.
curatorNotes: Hardware had no microprocessors; game logic was hard-wired into transistor-transistor logic (TTL) circuits. Games were discrete analog and digital electronic circuits.

name: Golden Age of Arcades & 2nd Generation
description: Space Invaders sparks a global coin shortage in Japan. Pac-Man becomes a worldwide pop-culture phenomenon. At home, the Atari 2600 brings interchangeable ROM cartridges to millions.
curatorNotes: Arcade cabinets generated billions of dollars in quarters, sparking moral panics, dedicated gaming parlors, and the founding of legendary studios like Namco, Taito, and Konami.

name: The 1983 Crash & 8-Bit Renaissance
description: A flood of low-quality shovelware causes the North American console market to collapse by 97%. Nintendo rescues the industry with the Famicom/NES, establishing the modern game design playbook.
curatorNotes: Nintendo introduced the Official Nintendo Seal of Quality, strict third-party publishing caps, and timeless character franchises led by Shigeru Miyamoto.

name: The 16-Bit Era & Console Wars
description: Sega launches 'Genesis does what Nintendon't' with Sonic the Hedgehog, triggering fierce commercial rivalry. The Game Boy dominates portables, while Street Fighter II revolutionizes fighting games.
curatorNotes: Pixel art reached its zenith. Sound chips transitioned from primitive beeps to multi-channel stereo FM synthesis and sampled instruments (SNES SPC700).

name: The 3D Revolution & CD-ROM Era
description: Sony enters gaming with the CD-based PlayStation, dethroning incumbent cartridge giants. Super Mario 64 invents the 3D camera grammar, Doom fuels PC LAN culture, and Final Fantasy VII proves games can rival Hollywood.
curatorNotes: Real-time 3D polygon pipelines replaced 2D sprites. Optical discs allowed gigabytes of cinematic FMV and orchestral audio, dramatically shifting game tone toward mature storytelling.

name: Sixth Generation & Dawn of Online
description: Sony's PlayStation 2 becomes the bestselling console in history. Microsoft enters with the Xbox and Xbox Live. Open-world games like GTA III change gaming forever, while World of Warcraft and Half-Life 2 reshape the PC landscape.
curatorNotes: Gaming became the highest-grossing entertainment sector, surpassing the Hollywood box office. Broadband internet transformed consoles into social multiplayer hubs.

name: HD Era & The Indie Explosion
description: High definition visuals arrive with Xbox 360 and PS3, while Nintendo's motion-controlled Wii engages non-gamers globally. Digital distribution fosters an unprecedented indie gaming renaissance (Minecraft, Braid, Limbo).
curatorNotes: Budgets for AAA titles skyrocketed past $100M, while solo creators built global sensations. Mobile platforms (iOS and Android) democratized touchscreen gaming.

name: Connected Worlds & Cinematic Depth
description: The PS4, Xbox One, and hybrid Nintendo Switch deliver sprawling open worlds with photo-realistic rendering and emotional narrative depth. Battle royales, live-service models, and esports break into global mainstream culture.
curatorNotes: Games like The Witcher 3, Breath of the Wild, and Red Dead Redemption 2 raised bar for player freedom, reactive physics, and simulated ecosystems.

name: The Modern Era & The Future
description: Hardware-accelerated ray tracing, instantaneous SSD load times, hand-held PC powerhouses (Steam Deck), and massive narrative achievements (Baldur's Gate 3, Elden Ring, Black Myth: Wukong) propel the medium toward its next golden age.
curatorNotes: We stand in the current era: boundary-pushing simulation, photorealistic global illumination, portable PC ecosystems, and anticipation for monumental generation-defining releases.
